subject.title: Bug: Orphaned TaskFlows in `waiting` status permanently block agent heartbeats (requests-in-flight deadlock)

question: Should OpenClaw add default TaskFlow wait-abandonment semantics, and what owner/deadline/proof should be required before a `waiting` flow can become terminal automatically?
rationale: The current API intentionally supports durable plugin-managed waits, while the reported unattended deadlock needs recovery; choosing the default timeout, owner signal, and runtime recovery path is a product/API compatibility decision that automation should not invent.

options.title: Define explicit wait ownership
options.body: Add controller-visible deadline or orphan metadata, then recover only flows that satisfy that contract and prove gateway heartbeat release with live diagnostics.

options.title: Keep this manual-repair only
options.body: Document `tasks audit` and a future doctor or maintenance repair path without changing default runtime semantics for existing plugin waits.

options.title: Pause until live busy-state proof
options.body: Require a current-main gateway reproduction that identifies whether TaskFlow state, pending final delivery, reply runs, or session lanes are the lasting `requests-in-flight` owner before choosing the fix shape.

recommendation.title: Define explicit wait ownership
recommendation.body: Add controller-visible deadline or orphan metadata, then recover only flows that satisfy that contract and prove gateway heartbeat release with live diagnostics.

likelyOwner.reason: Vincent has the clearest recent history across TaskFlow maintenance and the adjacent heartbeat retry boundary.
